limitations: One reverse-order pair, not a stable slowdown estimate.
Identical saved guest state does not ensure identical live cache after restore checks or equal host cache state.
128 MiB is a ceiling target, not a forced fill. Periodic clean-file traversal is not LRU or a hard limit.
Device reads cover the controller window, including preparation/stop/monitoring, not host disk reads.
Control physical points have guest metadata intervals inside control; host queries may extend beyond them. Unknown guest and provider quantities remain separate.
First lifecycle includes prefix creation/save; second skips them. Compare suffix timing, not whole lifecycle.
Both stop owned guest DAMON only while controlling, then restore it for official checks; no controller-off baseline.
Private service restarted from a verified full-volume backup before 128 MiB after a slot-metadata filename collision; same checkpoint and binaries, host warm state not matched.
scope: One actual checkpoint reused for 64 then 128 MiB; descriptive comparison after recovery, not matched initial cache or host cache.

failure_recovery.cause: Old released observation files use PID/device/queue/slot names. Recreating the same device in the same daemon hit create_new EEXIST; 16 slot tasks exited and the RPC timed out at 30 seconds.
failure_recovery.mitigation: Archive old observation metadata only after controller/samplers/guests stop and every slot is released; preserve originals without overwriting.
failure_recovery.backup_integrity: Full decompression SHA-256 matches source; original FAIL retained.
failure_recovery.no_restart_fixed_sequence_validation: Offline lifecycle test only; completed pair used explicit full-volume recovery.
